title: Dual Point of View
contribution: A joint textbook chapter that reads column generation as a cutting-plane method in the dual, proves the best Lagrangian bound equal to the Dantzig-Wolfe master bound, treats the subgradient method as a heuristic, and turns dual information into exact accelerators (dual-optimal inequalities, dual boxes, stabilized column generation with convergence propositions, hybrids), illustrated on a toy and on results reproduced from GERAD studies.
problem_entry: Enters from the question of what column generation, a primal algorithm, does in the dual space, and from the statement that Lagrangian relaxation is dual to Dantzig-Wolfe, framed by the Madsen (dual) versus Desrosiers (primal) anecdote; the motivating phenomena are oscillating duals in degenerate masters and the observed speed of dual boxes (pp. 4-5, 12, 48).
key_idea: Column generation is Kelley-Cheney-Goldstein cutting planes on the dual and pricing is dual separation, so the Lagrangian dual has the master's bound, and any exact restriction of the dual to its relevant region (dual-optimal inequalities, boxes, penalized trust regions) can speed up column generation while keeping optimality under stated conditions (pp. 5-6, 17, 39, 50-54).
assumptions: Pure ILP, feasible with finite optimum, constraints split into a linking set A and a pricing domain D (bounded for the subgradient method); exactness of a dual box needs an optimal dual strictly inside it; structures: set-partitioning/covering masters, cutting stock, multi-commodity MDVSP, GAP, capacitated p-median, VRPTW, edge coloring, 1-tree TSP, PCB assignment; data: a toy, ten random cutting-stock instances, one MDVSP instance, tsp225, manufacturer data; MILP only in an exercise; no MIPLIB (pp. 5, 10, 29, 39-40, 44-45, 50-51, 59-81, 89-91).
proof_devices: Prop 6.1 weak Lagrangian duality: re-add the relaxed rows and drop a non-positive penalty term (p. 12)

Prop 6.2 z_LDP = z_MP: rewrite the max-min as an LP with an epigraph variable and recognize the dual of the alternative master obtained by the affine change of variables mu = b'pi_b + pi_0 (pp. 9-10, 17); a second proof keeps b'pi_b as an offset and recovers the original master's dual (Note 6.6, pp. 17-18)
Prop 6.3 and Cor 6.1: optimal master duals solve the Lagrangian dual; convexity duals recovered for one block or identical blocks (p. 18)

Prop 6.5 Lagrangian function as the pointwise minimum of finitely many affine functions (p. 21), or as the boundary of an LP's hypograph (Note 6.10, p. 22); Prop 6.6 every pricing optimum gives a subgradient (p. 22)

Props 6.7-6.8 optimality by a zero subgradient, or by an ILP-feasible pricing optimum with complementary slackness, which follows from feasibility only for relaxed equalities; two-variable counterexample (pp. 25-26)

Props 6.9-6.10 dual boxes: weak and strong duality when the box contains an optimal dual, complementary slackness when one lies in the open box (p. 39); Prop 6.11 closed-form objective of the slack-and-surplus start (p. 43)

Cor 6.3 and Props 6.12-6.14 stabilized column generation: bounds by weak duality, strict improvement by a case split on the trust region's interior, convergence by contradiction on the limit of an increasing sequence (pp. 50, 53-54); [reading] the written proof of Prop 6.14 argues on the limit and assumes the limit point eventually lies inside the trust region, the step to finitely many iterations is not spelled out (p. 54)

Prop 6.15 Held-Karp 1-tree bound by invariance of tour costs under node-potential shifts (p. 72); subtour constraints on the complement made redundant by double counting degree sums (Note 6.23, pp. 69-71)

Algorithm 6.1 subgradient with the Polyak step, epsilon halved after three non-improving iterations, a heuristic by its stopping rules (pp. 30-31); initial epsilon in (0.75, 1) derived analytically for the toy (p. 32)

Algorithm 6.2 stabilized column generation: shrink the trust region and raise penalties when the dual is inside, recenter, enlarge and lower them when outside, or update on serious steps; stop at zero reduced cost with all auxiliary variables zero; final penalty constraints are deep dual-optimal inequalities (pp. 51-52)
Exercise 6.11 reduced-cost fixing with a dual box: fix x_j = 0 when its reduced cost at pi* exceeds sum_i delta_i |a_ij| (p. 89)
experiments: No new campaign: hand-computed toys plus results reproduced from cited studies, with no hardware, LP solver or time limit stated: ten random 501-item cutting-stock triplet instances, averages only (dual boxes: 124.2 to 12.2 iterations, 20.7 to 7.9 s, larger per-iteration time); one MDVSP instance with 4 depots and 800 trips (boxes at the known optimal duals: 4,178 s down to 37 s, radius 0.01 too tight and 0.4 below the optimum; stabilization from estimated duals: 439 s, about 10 times faster, RMP share 75 % to 49 %); Held-Karp bounds on tsp225 (LB 3876.85, UB 4111, optimum 3916); PCB lines on an IBM PC 286 (gaps 2.01-2.49 %); perfect-information caveat raised and answered; small text-table slips (pp. 40-47, 52-53, 70, 75, 80).
positioning: Lineage Kelley and Cheney-Goldstein, Geoffrion, Fisher, Magnanti et al. (1976), Marsten's boxstep, du Merle et al. (1999) and Ben Amor et al. (2006b, 2009), the last three with Desrosiers, plus bundle methods; re-reads Held and Karp (1970) for its much less known column-generation half; concedes branch-and-cut for large TSPs; cites Lübbecke's own work only as Gauthier et al. (2016, 2018) on degenerate LPs; sends readers to Gurobi for quadratic stabilization (pp. 5, 24, 48, 55, 59, 71, 76, 85-86; S017 text file pp. 660-668).
writing: Joint textbook voice with an epigraph, a 1993 parody song, joke note titles and photographs; one toy (TCSPP) carried through every view with each coincidence flagged; questions raised, answered and re-asked as exercises; misconceptions corrected; notation chosen to carry the duality claim; hedges and untested questions labelled (pp. 1, 4, 9, 12, 14-15, 18-19, 24, 33, 74-76, 88).
limits_future: No theory of how to split constraints or of what a good decomposition means (p. 19); subgradient is a heuristic without primal output and with unpredictable convergence (pp. 29, 31, 33); perfect dual information is unlikely and dual heuristics are insufficiently studied (p. 57); tiny boxes fail numerically (p. 46); four Held-Karp column-generation questions never tested (p. 76); future: dynamic refinement of box radius and center (p. 47), a self-adjusting rule for delta and epsilon (Exercise 6.10, p. 88).

method_links.note: The compact ILP stays the object; the bound chain (6.32) with Cor 6.2(b) restates the no-gain case (integrality property gives z_LP), and the examples apply it per grouping before any computation (GAP semi-assignment relaxation gives knapsacks and a possible gain, capacity relaxation gives none; likewise cutting stock, edge coloring, 1-tree, PCB assignment). Also H1 evidence: every column-generation iteration yields a Lagrangian bound for early termination (Note 6.7, p. 19), a 53.3 % gap sends the toy to the search tree (p. 26), and duals from a few subgradient iterations replace a degenerate RMP re-optimization (pp. 57-58); H1 qualification: the free bound needs exact or relaxed pricing, heuristic pricing gives none (Note 6.11, p. 24); H6 evidence: an objective below the known optimum read as a too-tight box and a precision limit (p. 46), updates counted in the data, not the plot (p. 52); Taste G1 evidence: every proposition proved and every heuristic output given with its gap (pp. 26, 32, 75, 80); Misreading 3 evidence: branch-and-cut credited for large TSPs (p. 71), Lagrangian relaxation alone suffices in some applications (p. 59).

Step 4 (probe before you build) gets a cheaper probe: the Lagrangian dual has the master's bound and a subgradient run needs no master implementation, but it is a heuristic lower approximation without primal output (Example 6.6: 6, -8, 0.125, 5.5, 4.125 against z_LP = 7). Step 2's yardstick is absent: no timed comparison runs the compact model in a MILP solver; the baseline is always plain column generation.

As an explanation device: all nine TCSPP paths enumerated, the whole Lagrangian function drawn with breakpoints and subdifferentials, with the warning that such enumeration is impossible in practice; Note 6.8 states there is no theory of a good split and offers Lagrangian experience as a second source for choosing master constraints.

Failures and costs reported (larger per-iteration time, radius 0.01 too tight, harder first problem after an update), the perfect-information caveat raised and answered with estimated duals, and data trusted over the plot; but every timed number is borrowed from cited studies (two co-authored by Desrosiers), on ten random instances (averages) or one instance, without hardware, LP solver or time limit; general advice that good duals help whichever variant rests on two illustrations; a modern-hardware speed estimate is not re-run; two numbers differ between text and table or figure. Random instances illustrate a mechanism here, not a benchmark claim (cf. warning sign B2). Also Workflow G step 3 variant: with the RMP at 75 % of the time, stabilization cut total time by 89 %, and the dual-side hybrid is tied to masters costly relative to pricing (pp. 52, 58); Workflow C step 3 evidence: master/pricing split measured (pp. 41, 52).

One notation for Dantzig-Wolfe and Lagrangian objects; a common misconception corrected; open questions published (no theory of good decompositions, dynamic boxes in the making, dual heuristics insufficient, LP-bound equality unclear, four untested Held-Karp questions); the much less known column-generation half of Held and Karp (1970) recovered; the authors were tempted several times to forward-reference this chapter while writing the book. Step 1: unstable duals that his static stabilization did not fix in the 2001 thesis code (card S027, pp. 139-140, 142) get their systematic answer here.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Explain a column-generation behaviour by its dual meaning before tuning it
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Each primal-side effect gets a dual reading that predicts it: iterations are dual cuts and pricing is dual separation; heuristic pricing over-approximates the Lagrangian function (no valid bound) while relaxed pricing cuts into it (valid bound); dual boxes stop cuts in irrelevant dual regions; columns of an integer start solution act as misleading dual bounds, so such a start can be worse than none; artificial-variable costs are dual bounds; the final stabilization constraints are deep dual-optimal inequalities; a subgradient step predicts which customers the next pricing round favours.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Seed the duals, not only the columns
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Closed-form optimal duals for cutting-stock triplets cut iterations from 124.2 to 12.2; boxes around the MDVSP's known optimal duals cut time from 4,178 s to between 37 and 836 s; estimated duals from an aggregated single-depot flow problem give about a 10-fold speed-up; removal-savings and insertion-cost estimates give a dual box for routing; artificial penalties should be dual estimates; the literature on dual heuristics is called clearly insufficient.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Pick the accelerator by the measured master/pricing time split
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Every timed table reports the RMP share of time (90/10 down to 6/94 in cutting stock; 75/25 to 49/51 in the MDVSP); stabilization is motivated by degenerate RMPs; a few subgradient iterations are recommended instead of re-optimizing the RMP when it is difficult or time consuming relative to pricing; SKILL.md's Workflow G places stabilization last by inference only.

transferable: Dual box as two columns per row: a surplus y1 with cost -delta1 and a slack y2 with cost delta2; start the RMP with no generated columns; accept the lambda-part as a master optimum only when y1 = y2 = 0, which an optimal dual strictly inside the box guarantees (Props 6.10-6.11, pp. 39, 43).

Radius sweep: run the box at radii infinity, 100, 10, 1, 0.1, 0.01 and tabulate final and initial objective, time, iterations, columns, pivots; a final objective below the known optimum marks a box too tight or too small for the arithmetic (Table 6.6, pp. 45-46).

Stabilized column-generation loop: if the dual is inside the trust region shrink it and raise the penalties, otherwise recenter, enlarge and lower them, or update only on a serious step that raises the Lagrangian bound; stop at zero reduced cost with every auxiliary variable at zero (Algorithm 6.2, (6.78), pp. 51-52).

Dual estimates without solving: in a set-partitioning routing master, bound a customer's dual by the savings of removing it from its route and by the cost of inserting it once more (or of a new vehicle); in a multi-depot problem take the duals of the aggregated single-depot network-flow problem (pp. 52, 57-58).
Set artificial-variable penalties to dual estimates instead of a big-M: each penalty bounds a dual variable, and smaller penalties restrict the dual space more (p. 58).

Cutting-stock dual-optimal inequalities: with items sorted by width, add m - 1 zero-cost exchange columns (ranking inequalities pi_{i+1} <= pi_i) to the RMP and swap them out of the final solution to recover a master solution (pp. 36-37).

Smoothed duals with a mis-price check: price at a convex combination of the stability center and the RMP duals (Wentges 1997); if nothing prices out there, check the RMP duals before stopping (pp. 55-56).

Subgradient start: keep every subgradient's column (its cost and b - a_p) for the first RMP; for VRPTW-type pricing start the multipliers at 0 and raise them slowly, which keeps adjusted costs positive and avoids cycles in labelling; derive the step parameter's scale on a small case and halve it after three non-improving iterations (Fig. 6.14, Algorithm 6.1, pp. 31-32, 34, 57).
Reduced-cost fixing from a dual box: fix x_j = 0 when its reduced cost at pi* exceeds sum_i delta_i |a_ij| (Exercise 6.11, p. 89).

Integrality-property screen per candidate grouping before decomposing: in the generalized assignment problem, relaxed semi-assignment rows give knapsack pricing and a possible bound gain, relaxed capacities give an integral problem and no gain (pp. 60-61).

Run one toy instance through every view of the method (primal iterations, dual cuts, Lagrangian function, subgradient, boxed master) and say each time which observation is an artefact of its size (pp. 9, 24, 33).
coauthors: Jacques Desrosiers, Guy Desaulniers, Jean Bertrand Gauthier (book co-authors; joint voice; Desrosiers's initials sign one epigraph, p. 43)

quotes.text: The dual variables are the secret stars in the column generation algorithm. They determine which columns are generated and when we stop.
We do not even know what “good” in this context generally means.
